The UN treated the earlier Iran sanctions resolutions as reapplied from 27 September 2025 at 8 p.m. Eastern Time, equivalent to 28 September UTC. BNM's 22 December 2025 circular instructed relevant Malaysian institutions on implementation. These targeted proliferation, financial and related restrictions are not a blanket embargo on every Iranian crude shipment. Sources: https://main.un.org/securitycouncil/en/content/2231/background ; https://main.un.org/securitycouncil/en/sanctions/1737 ; https://www.malaysianbar.org.my/cms/upload_files/document/Circular%20No%20005-2026.pdf .

Malaysian measures did not stop with the June commencement. Marine Sensitive Area Notice MSA 01/2026 was issued on 10 September and became effective on 11 September 2026, adding controls for a defined area. This is relevant to the governance chronology. Source: https://www.mkn.gov.my/web/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2026/09/Marine-Sensitive-Area-Notice.pdf .

National rejection of unilateral sanctions does not mean banks disregard them. BNM's financial-institution FAQ says decisions concerning persons on unilateral sanctions lists depend on each institution's assessment and risk appetite. This helps explain why banking scrutiny can matter independently of a minister's general foreign-policy position. Source, checked 8 November 2026: https://amlcft.bnm.gov.my/faq/tfs-fi/targeted-financial-sanctions .

UN Comtrade explains that mirror-trade differences can arise from partner attribution, timing, warehousing, valuation and other methodological differences. The enormous discrepancy warrants investigation, but the dataset alone cannot allocate it to fraud, Iranian origin or any particular operator. Likewise, Malaysia's reported 0.31 Mt of exports does not itself prove Malaysian geological origin or exclude re-exports. Source: https://uncomtrade.org/docs/exports-of-a-country-not-coincide-with-imports-of-its-partner/ .

Treasury itself recognizes that ship-to-ship transfers are a legitimate commercial practice that can be misused. A transfer, a Malaysian connection or an origin label alone is not proof of sanctions evasion. Source: Treasury sb0322, 20 November 2025, https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0322 .

Kpler expressly distinguished its October 2026 analysts' oil-on-water estimate from platform figures awaiting discharge updates. Omitting that methodological caveat makes the apparent precision of 'zero' stronger than its source supports. Source: https://www.kpler.com/blog/irans-oil-on-water-outside-the-blockade-zone-hits-zero-as-tehrans-trilemma-sharpens , 22 October 2026. This is a verified feature of the published estimate, not independent primary validation of the inventory.

MMEA's inspected January 2026 release establishes a detention relating to suspected unauthorized transfer and anchoring, but does not establish Iranian cargo origin. Its detention evidence should not be used as another verified Iranian-oil case without the subsequent investigation or court record. Source: https://www.mmea.gov.my/eng/index.php/en/12-berita-utama/3283-53-kru-bersama-dua-kapal-tangki-ditahan-cuba-pindah-minyak-mentah-bernilai-lebih-rm512-juta , 31 January 2026.
source_assessment: The consolidated bibliography contains approximately 23 documentary or dataset items: one Comtrade dataset family, two EIA items, one gazette, three Treasury releases, two OFAC items, two FinCEN publications, one CGEP article, seven dated Reuters reports, and one item each from Bernama, TASS, Kpler and Al Jazeera. These represent 12 named publishing bodies or platforms, or 10 institutional groups when Treasury, OFAC and FinCEN are consolidated. This is not 23 independent lines of evidence: Reuters republications are the same reporting, UN-hosted national submissions are not independent corroboration of those submissions, and EIA's reuse of GAC figures does not create another independent customs measurement. The strongest material is official statistical, legal and regulatory documentation. The institutional range also includes international commercial journalism, a US university policy centre, commercial shipping analysts, Malaysian public news reporting, a Russian state news agency and a Qatar-based news organization. Security attribution remains concentrated in US sanctions institutions; Malaysian policy voices mostly arrive through news reports. Direct cargo records, original analyst methodology, Malaysian case-disposition documents, affected operators' responses and substantive Chinese or Iranian responses to the specific discrepancy are missing. Argus, Energy Aspects and China's MOFA add voices outside the consolidated bibliography, but their document-level citations are incomplete. Iran International is explicitly excluded from the cards and should not count as an opposition source supporting them. The diversity estimate of 0.58 is a qualitative assessment of institutional and evidentiary breadth, not a statistical measurement or a requirement to balance verified arithmetic with partisan opinion. Under the requested restrictive definition, accurately attributed news quotations and proprietary analyst estimates remain UNVERIFIED where their underlying primary evidence was not separately inspected.
overall_assessment: Checked as of 8 November 2026, using the analysis's 7 November SDN download as its apparent time reference. The central 2025 customs discrepancy, the 206-fold weight ratio, the stated EIA observations, the principal Treasury and FinCEN attributions, and the EEZ commencement date are well supported. The 2026 strikes and blockade chronology are also supported by contemporary official documents and should not be rejected as implausibly recent. Publication nevertheless requires material revisions: correct the sanctions count to at least eleven within the stated broad scope; qualify the EEZ rule's legal scope; disclose the conflicting DOSM production series and 2024 trade figure; replace ownership and strict-provenance conclusions with clearly stated inferences; and update the sanctions-policy context and dated case status. Several precise ministerial, monthly-trade and analyst claims remain unverified under the user's required standard, despite matching reputable published reporting. The 76/100 score is an editorial assessment of evidentiary support and material defects, not a computed probability or a claim that every UNVERIFIED item is false. The reporting-discrepancy story is substantially supported; a fully established account of the origin, ownership, location and legal status of the underlying cargoes is not.
